summary.headline: Zydus Wellness Q4 FY26 net sales grew 62.1% on Comfort Click, but net profit fell 5.8% as seasonal brands dropped 9.8% in the domestic business.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales rose 62.1% YoY, driven by the Comfort Click acquisition, with international like-to-like growth of 31.4% and domestic growth of only 1.7%. Domestic seasonal brands fell 9.8% as a delayed summer and rain in March and mid-April left retail and wholesale pipelines unfilled, while skin and hair care rose 39.7% and food and nutrition rose 9.4%. EBITDA grew 42.2% to INR 2,701 million, but net profit fell 5.8% due to higher finance costs from the acquisition debt, higher amortization of acquired brands and exceptional items. Management said operating leverage and the 17-18% EBITDA margin goal remain intact, while the seasonal recovery is expected from May onwards.

financial_highlights.metric: International incl. Comfort Click like-to-like growth (Q4)

financial_highlights.change: Seasonal -9.8%, skin and hair care +39.7%, food and nutrition +9.4%
Excluding exceptional items and amortization of acquired brands: +17%
Excluding exceptional items and amortization of acquired brands: +2.3%

segments.name: Seasonal brands (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 declined 9.8% and FY26 declined 18.8%; management attributed it to a delayed summer, March/April rains in the East and North, and missed retailer pipeline build. Seasonal carries above-average gross margin and EBITDA, so its weakness diluted the mix.

segments.name: Skin and hair care (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 39.7% and FY26 grew 21.9%. Everyuth grew at strong double digits in FY26 and Cuticolor has been in the portfolio for about six months, sold in organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce.

segments.name: Food and nutrition (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 9.4% and FY26 grew 15.5%. RiteBite Max Protein grew at roughly 50% in FY26 (about INR 244 crore per analyst), and management said actual branded growth is higher than reported due to contract manufacturing optimization.

segments.name: International incl. Comfort Click
segments.commentary: Like-to-like growth of 31.4% in Q4 and 29.5% in FY26. Comfort Click has been held for seven months; it is EPS accretive on a standalone basis in Q4, and the total-to-constant-currency gap is about 3%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a recovery in seasonal brands from May onwards, and hopes some early-season misses can be recovered if summer progresses normally; it declined to forecast the full season.
Seasonal brands are expected to deliver consistent double-digit growth over three to four years, per management.
EBITDA margin aspiration of 17-18% reiterated for the next couple of years, measured excluding Comfort Click.
Comfort Click EPS accretive from Q4; management maintained its earlier guidance for the next two years.
Tax rate: FY26-27 is a mix of cash tax and deferred tax asset utilisation; FY27-28 is expected at about 25%, and FY28 at full cash tax.
Operating leverage expected to play out across the business excluding Comfort Click, which has largely variable spend.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.

Launch activity in Q4: Max Protein Ultimate RTD, Max Protein Roots Ghee Jaggery Bar and Korean flavour chips; Sugar Free D'lite Choco Spread; Everyuth Tan Removal Face Wash; Glucon-D Recharge (liquid and sachets); seven Comfort Click launches across WeightWorld and Animigo.
Complan NutriGro was relaunched and moved to direct supply in the kids segment; VieMax by Complan launched in adult nutrition.
Channel expansion: Boots.com (UK) for WeightWorld and MaxMedix; Amazon UAE for vitamins and supplements.
Management said no divestments are planned, and capital allocation across brands is considered appropriate.
demand_pricing: Rural demand recovery continued to outpace the gradual urban improvement; quick commerce and e-commerce growth remained strong.
Quick commerce is about 7-8% of total domestic business; e-commerce is about 44-45% of organized trade.
Sugar Free Green reported its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth; sweetener market share rose 24 bps (MAT March 2026); Nutralite grew at double digits despite gas supply headwinds.
Management said supply disruption from the Middle East conflict has been limited, affecting only a very small part of the business.
Gross margins were in line with plan; management cited brand-level margin improvements and exits from low-margin products.

qa_highlights.question: What weighed on seasonal growth and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak North and East markets, March/April rains, and a missing retailer pipeline build ahead of summer. It expects a recovery from May onwards but declined to forecast the season.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be expected to move toward the 17-18% aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins are in line with plan and the miss was driven by mix from weak seasonal sales. Umesh Parikh said operating leverage will play out across the business excluding Comfort Click.

qa_highlights.question: Is quick commerce changing the innovation and channel approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said the portfolio is designed for quick commerce consumers while keeping the traditional channel SKUs. Quick commerce is about 7-8% of domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Comfort Click margin trajectory and is it EPS accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Umesh Parikh said Comfort Click is in line with or slightly ahead of expectations, and it became EPS accretive in Q4. The currency tailwind is about 3%, the gap between reported and constant-currency growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company divest slow-growing categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said there are no plans to divest any category and no major change in capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cuticolor gaining traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Cuticolor is positioned as a derma-backed, Korean-origin safe hair colour sold in organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce, with repeat buying and early traction, after about six months in the portfolio.

risks_watch: Seasonal recovery depends on May-June temperatures and rainfall; a further weak season would hit the margin mix and FY27 growth.
Domestic growth was only 1.7% in Q4 and 2.4% in FY26, with the seasonal decline masking growth in the rest of the portfolio.
Net profit fell 5.8% in Q4 and 43.2% in FY26 despite EBITDA growth, as finance costs, amortization of acquired brands and exceptional items rose. Watch the tax mix in FY27.
Comfort Click's growth depends on European online VMS demand, FX (GBP/EUR) and the supply chain; the US and UAE are early-stage bets.
Watch whether the 17-18% EBITDA margin target is reached without Comfort Click, given that management gave no new timeline.
Management declined to disclose RiteBite and Nutralite brand-level growth and category data, and geographic segment disclosure is still under consideration.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long term and on Comfort Click and RiteBite, but defensive on the near term: it attributed the seasonal miss to external weather and channel timing and gave no new margin timeline. Management avoided quantifying several questions, including brand-level growth, Comfort Click EBITDA and the timing of the margin target.
key_quotes: So our margins at a gross margin level has actually in line with what we have planned.
It's not about that we have to clean up every time. It is just that the pipeline buildup, which is in anticipation of summers, as the summer kick in, they start buying in advance.
So I think if we segment the portfolio, this concern remains. But now if you look at the new portfolio and as the expanded portfolio, the saliency of this business has reduced.
I think there are no new numbers. We've talked about in the next couple of years, we hope to get to our 17-18.

growth.why: Management guides to a seasonal recovery from May and reiterates a 17-18% EBITDA margin ex Comfort Click, with seasonal brands expected to grow double digits over three to four years, but no capacity, capex or utilisation was discussed and backing is largely qualitative (launches, channel expansion, operating leverage).
